channel.title: The Melbourne Indian
channel.description: Independent, free-to-read news for Melbourne's Indian communities in English, Hindi and Punjabi.

item.title: From Thursday, Training visas can only be applied for from outside Australia
item.description: Anyone in Melbourne hoping to move onto a subclass 407 Training visa will have to leave the country first, the Department of Home Affairs says.

item.title: Victoria's skilled visa nomination is open again for the 190 visa, but not yet for the regional 491
item.description: If you hoped for Victorian state nomination this year, you need a fresh registration of interest. Here is what is confirmed, and what to check.

item.title: Liberals drop Williamstown candidate Paul Lindemann over comments about Indigenous Australians, but his name stays on the ballot
item.description: The party says it was not aware of the comments before. Nominations have closed, so he will still appear on ballot papers in the Labor-held seat.

item.title: At Gallipoli, the ANZACs weren't alone: the Indian soldiers Remembrance Day forgets
item.description: Around 16,000 soldiers from India served at Gallipoli in 1915, and at least 12 Indian Australians joined the AIF despite a law that said they couldn't. This year, nearly 10,000 more Indian soldiers of the First World War were finally added to the official records.

item.title: Big Build inquiry: ex-CFMEU organiser says Mick Gatto gave him a gold bracelet, and agrees 11 union officials had bikie links
item.description: On the third day of hearings, a former organiser told the royal commission that the underworld figure sometimes stepped in for employers, and that WorkSafe gave the Sunbury site occupation its lowest priority.

item.title: David Jones to close 19 stores, including Highpoint, Glen Waverley and Malvern Central
item.description: Receivers say an urgent restructure is needed. Most closing stores are in the suburbs; city flagships largely survive.

item.title: Ramayana wins Australia's box office election in a landslide
item.description: Victorians vote on 28 November, but cinemagoers have already declared a winner: the Hindi epic topped the national box office, with Godzilla second, the first time two non-English films have led an Australian weekend.

item.title: Eleven First World War soldiers buried as 'unknown' are named, five of them from Victoria
item.description: Men from Preston, Brunswick, Melbourne, Lilydale and Ballarat are among the Diggers identified through research, archaeology and DNA, announced on Remembrance Day.

item.title: Police divers join search for missing 17-year-old in Gippsland bush, now in its fifth day
item.description: William, who goes by Will, was last seen on Friday afternoon while camping near Walhalla East. Police say they are still hopeful.

item.title: Qantas to cut 850 corporate jobs, with most of the work moving to Accenture in India
item.description: Finance, procurement, HR and marketing staff are first in line. Qantas blames clunky systems and AI; unions call it offshoring, and the Acting Prime Minister says it is disappointing.

item.title: Coalition will put Labor and the Greens below One Nation on how-to-vote cards, Jess Wilson confirms
item.description: The Opposition Leader says Labor, the Greens and the Socialists will go last on Coalition cards, decided seat by seat. Labor calls it a deal; the Greens are angry at Labor's own call in Prahran.

item.title: Police investigating temple power cuts in Melbourne's west, appeal for dashcam footage
item.description: Victoria Police says it has not yet determined whether the two incidents at the Swaminarayan temple before Diwali were racially or religiously motivated.

item.title: Inside the Big Build inquiry: what two days of hearings have revealed, and what comes before Victorians vote
item.description: A $6 million stoppage, a rail site taken over and contractor memos about union access to ministers. Here is what the royal commission has heard so far, what is disputed, and what still has to be answered.

item.title: Cricket Australia won't reopen ball-tampering inquiry despite Khawaja's claims
item.description: Chief executive Todd Greenberg says parts of Usman Khawaja's book contradict other accounts, and he sees no reason to revisit the 2018 Cape Town scandal.

item.title: One Nation drops its Preston candidate over social media posts praising Hitler, but his name stays on the ballot
item.description: Franco Guardiani confirmed the accounts were his. Nominations had already closed, so he will still appear under the One Nation name in the Labor-held seat.

item.title: Khawaja's book reopens Cape Town ball-tampering row, and Warner says his account is accurate
item.description: Usman Khawaja writes that the whole touring party knew about the 2018 plan and that Victoria were the Shield's best at the 'dark arts'. Scott Boland says he has seen nothing untoward.

item.title: Australia-India Maitri grants and fellowships open for 2026-27
item.description: Community groups, businesses, universities and sporting bodies with an India link can apply for funding for exchanges and joint projects.

item.title: Victoria's prisons are 92 per cent full, and both major parties are promising to lock up more people
item.description: With law and order at the centre of the 28 November election, experts say neither Labor nor the Coalition has said how many extra prison beds their policies will need, or what they will cost.

item.title: Melbourne data centre expansion halted as power delays and community opposition bite
item.description: NEXTDC has paused every project without a signed customer after residents in Melbourne's west stopped the power upgrade its West Footscray site needs. Its chief executive says the company has to win back trust first.

item.title: $450,000 raised for family of delivery rider Feng Jianming as man faces murder charge
item.description: Melbourne has rallied behind the father of two killed near Queen Victoria Market. A 51-year-old man appeared in court on Monday, and police say they are flooding the CBD with officers.

item.title: Labuschagne left out for New Zealand Tests, but selectors keep the door open for India
item.description: Australia's selectors say the 49-innings century drought calls for 'a little bit of space'. A return for the India tour in January is 'still possible, absolutely'.

item.title: Indian students could have to park tens of thousands of dollars in an Australian bank before they can apply for a visa
item.description: Home Affairs is weighing a shake-up of student visa money rules, with a tougher interim check aimed at countries including India. Families have until 23 November to have their say.

item.title: Big Build inquiry: union stoppage added $6m to Sunbury rail job, and 'every dollar' was paid first by the state, counsel says
item.description: The royal commission's first day laid out how a two-day stoppage at Gap Road played out. The first witnesses are due to give evidence today. None of the allegations has been tested.

item.title: Vandals cut power to a temple in Melbourne's west on the eve of Diwali, MPs say
item.description: The SMVS Swaminarayan temple near Tarneit lost power twice in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. Labor has pledged $200,000 for its security if re-elected.

item.title: Victorian election: who is standing in the seven districts with the most India-born residents
item.description: Here are all 61 candidates standing in Tarneit, Laverton, Kalkallo, Point Cook, Cranbourne, Williamstown and Thomastown, in ballot-paper order, and how to fill in your ballot papers.

item.title: Coalition promises 'Aidan's Law' for people who step in to help, as Labor pledges more police at station counters
item.description: Jess Wilson says courts would have to treat an attack on a Good Samaritan as more serious if the Coalition wins on 28 November. Labor is promising 200 more police reservists.

item.title: India v Australia: the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy will start at 3pm Melbourne time
item.description: Five Tests in Nagpur, Chennai, Guwahati, Ranchi and Ahmedabad from 21 January, with Australia defending the trophy they won 3-1 at home.

item.title: Cricket this summer: the big matches in Melbourne, and when India play
item.description: England play a T20 at the MCG on 21 November, New Zealand are here for the Boxing Day Test, and India host Australia for five Tests from 21 January.

item.title: Cricket clubs can apply for a share of a new $900,000 fund to cut energy costs
item.description: Clubs, associations, schools and councils can seek grants for solar panels, batteries and other facility upgrades. Applications close on 26 February 2027.

item.title: Family visiting from India? Visa applicants there may now need to give fingerprints
item.description: Since 26 October, people applying for an Australian visa in India may be asked for fingerprints and a facial image. The Australian High Commission says applications lodged before that date are not affected.
